new_task_1.title: Remove built-in nose compatibility and plugin loading
new_task_1.description: Pytest 8.1.1 removes the built-in `nose` plugin and the compatibility hook paths that used to execute nose-style setup and teardown helpers, so suites that still rely on nose conventions must migrate to native pytest or unittest mechanisms.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure the upgrade no longer depends on pytest's built-in nose compatibility, including the bundled `nose` plugin and automatic execution of nose-style function setup and teardown helpers.

expectation.grounded: Pytest should no longer auto-load a `nose` default plugin, because `nose` has been removed from the default plugin list and `_pytest/nose.py` has been deleted. Function-level nose compatibility hooks that previously called `setup` and `teardown` attributes on collected test functions should no longer run. Test suites must rely on supported pytest fixtures/xunit hooks or unittest lifecycle methods instead.
expectation.conceptual: Projects upgrading to 8.1.1 need to stop depending on pytest to emulate nose behavior. Native pytest and unittest lifecycle support remains, but the old nose bridge is gone.

constraints.grounded: Do not change supported pytest fixture behavior or standard unittest lifecycle behavior such as `setUpClass`, `tearDownClass`, `setup_method`, and `teardown_method`. Do not assume the removed `nose` plugin can still be enabled with `-p nose` or through default plugin loading.
constraints.conceptual: Keep supported pytest and unittest flows working, but remove the legacy nose-specific execution path entirely.

behavior: Pytest no longer ships or auto-loads the built-in `nose` plugin.
Passing `-p nose` or otherwise depending on `_pytest.nose` is no longer supported.
Collected test functions no longer get nose-style `setup` and `teardown` helpers invoked through pytest's old nose compatibility hook.
Suites that previously relied on `nose.tools.with_setup` or equivalent function attributes must migrate to supported pytest fixtures or xunit hooks.
Standard pytest fixtures and supported unittest lifecycle hooks continue to be the intended execution model after the upgrade.
acceptance_criteria: When a suite upgrades to pytest 8.1.1, it should not rely on pytest auto-loading a built-in `nose` plugin.
When a test function only defines nose-style `setup` or `teardown` helpers through the removed compatibility path, pytest should no longer invoke those helpers automatically.
When a project previously enabled the bundled plugin with `-p nose`, that configuration should be treated as unsupported and migrated away.
When tests use supported pytest fixtures or supported unittest lifecycle methods instead of nose compatibility helpers, they should continue to work.

new_task_2.title: Drop deprecated plugin bootstrap and collector compatibility APIs
new_task_2.description: Pytest 8.1.1 removes several long-deprecated extension points and compatibility shims: `pytest_cmdline_preparse` is no longer part of the hook set, `pytest.Instance` is no longer exported, `FSCollector.gethookproxy()` and `FSCollector.isinitpath()` are gone, and option definitions must use modern argparse-compatible types and help placeholders.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure custom plugins, conftests, and collector integrations are migrated off deprecated bootstrap and collector APIs that pytest 8.1.1 no longer provides.

expectation.grounded: Pytest should no longer invoke `pytest_cmdline_preparse`, because its hookspec and explicit preparse call have been removed; extensions must use `pytest_load_initial_conftests` instead. The lazy `pytest.Instance` export has been removed from `pytest.__init__`, so that symbol is no longer provided through `pytest`. `FSCollector` no longer exposes `gethookproxy()` or `isinitpath()`, so callers must use `self.session.gethookproxy()` and `self.session.isinitpath()`. Argument parsing should no longer rewrite optparse-style string `type=` values or `%default` help placeholders into argparse-compatible forms automatically.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade removes compatibility layers for old plugin and collector APIs. Extensions now need to use the supported replacements directly instead of depending on pytest to translate or proxy deprecated patterns.

constraints.grounded: Preserve supported replacement APIs: `pytest_load_initial_conftests` for early command-line processing, `session.gethookproxy()` and `session.isinitpath()` for collector/session access, real Python type objects for option declarations, and modern argparse-style help text. Do not rely on deprecated aliases, lazy exports, or warning-based transition behavior that no longer exists.
constraints.conceptual: Supported extension points should remain intact, but deprecated shims should be treated as removed rather than merely warned about.

behavior: `pytest_cmdline_preparse` is no longer a supported or invoked pytest hook.
Early command-line customization must move to `pytest_load_initial_conftests`.
`pytest.Instance` is no longer exposed as a public lazy attribute on the `pytest` package.
`FSCollector.gethookproxy()` and `FSCollector.isinitpath()` are no longer available on collector instances.
Parser option declarations must provide modern argparse-compatible definitions instead of depending on pytest to normalize string `type=` values or `%default` help placeholders.
acceptance_criteria: When a plugin defines `pytest_cmdline_preparse`, pytest 8.1.1 should no longer depend on that hook being called to mutate startup arguments.
When a plugin needs early startup customization, implementing `pytest_load_initial_conftests` should remain the supported migration path.
When code accesses `pytest.Instance`, it should no longer rely on pytest exporting that deprecated symbol.
When collector code needs hook proxies or init-path checks, it should call the corresponding `session` methods instead of removed `FSCollector` helpers.
When a plugin declares custom CLI options, it should pass real type objects and already-correct help text instead of expecting pytest to rewrite deprecated optparse-style forms.

new_task_3.title: Reject `pytest.warns(None)` instead of treating it as a catch-all
new_task_3.description: Passing `None` to `pytest.warns()` is no longer accepted in 8.1.1. The deprecated catch-all form has been removed, and pytest now raises `TypeError` unless the expected warning argument is a `Warning` subclass or a tuple of them.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure warning assertions no longer rely on the deprecated `pytest.warns(None)` form after upgrading to pytest 8.1.1.

expectation.grounded: The `WarningsChecker` constructor should only accept a `Warning` subclass or a tuple of `Warning` subclasses as `expected_warning`. Passing `None` should no longer emit a deprecation warning and continue; it should now raise `TypeError` during `pytest.warns(None)` setup.
expectation.conceptual: Warning assertions must use an explicit warning type instead of a special `None` catch-all mode. Invalid `None` usage should fail immediately.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the normal behavior of `pytest.warns()` when given a valid warning class or tuple of warning classes. Only the deprecated `None` form should stop working.
constraints.conceptual: Keep valid warning assertions stable while removing the ambiguous deprecated shortcut.

behavior: Pytest no longer emits a deprecation warning and records warnings when `None` is passed.
Valid warning expectations such as `pytest.warns(UserWarning)` and tuples of warning classes continue to work.
The accepted `expected_warning` contract is now restricted to actual warning types.
acceptance_criteria: When code calls `pytest.warns(None)`, pytest should raise `TypeError` instead of returning a warnings recorder.
When code calls `pytest.warns(Warning)` or another warning subclass, pytest should continue to capture and validate warnings normally.
When code calls `pytest.warns((UserWarning, RuntimeWarning))`, pytest should continue to accept the tuple form.
When suites previously used `pytest.warns(None)` as a catch-all recorder, they should be migrated because that form is no longer supported.

new_task_4.title: Remove deprecated `msg=` aliases from pytest outcome helpers
new_task_4.description: Pytest 8.1.1 removes the deprecated `msg=` keyword compatibility from `pytest.skip()`, `pytest.fail()`, and `pytest.exit()`. Calls must use `reason=` where applicable, and `pytest.exit()` now allows an empty reason instead of requiring one.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure tests and helpers use the current pytest outcome-helper signatures after upgrading, without relying on the removed `msg=` alias behavior.

expectation.grounded: The public signatures for `pytest.skip()` and `pytest.fail()` should accept `reason` and no longer accept `msg`. `pytest.exit()` should accept `reason` and `returncode`, without the deprecated `msg` keyword or the old requirement that one of `reason` or `msg` must be provided. Calling `pytest.exit()` with no reason should now raise `Exit` with an empty reason rather than a `UsageError`.
expectation.conceptual: Outcome helpers now use a single modern argument style. Deprecated aliases are gone, and `pytest.exit()` behaves like a normal explicit termination helper even when no message is supplied.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing behavior for calls that already use `reason=` and, for `pytest.exit()`, `returncode=`. Do not keep compatibility code that maps `msg` to `reason` or that raises the old mixed-argument usage errors.
constraints.conceptual: Supported modern calls should keep working, while deprecated alias-based calls should be considered invalid after the upgrade.

behavior: `pytest.skip(msg=...)` is no longer supported; callers must use `reason=`.
`pytest.fail(msg=...)` is no longer supported; callers must use `reason=`.
`pytest.exit(msg=...)` is no longer supported; callers must use `reason=` if they want a message.
`pytest.exit()` without a message is now allowed and raises `Exit` with an empty reason.
Deprecated argument-reconciliation paths for mixing `reason` and `msg` have been removed along with the `msg` parameter itself.
acceptance_criteria: When code calls `pytest.skip(reason="...")`, `pytest.fail(reason="...")`, or `pytest.exit(reason="...")`, those calls should continue to work.
When code passes `msg=` to `pytest.skip()`, `pytest.fail()`, or `pytest.exit()`, it should no longer rely on pytest accepting that deprecated alias.
When code calls `pytest.exit()` with no arguments, pytest should terminate by raising `Exit` with an empty reason instead of raising `UsageError` for a missing message.
When code previously passed both `reason` and `msg`, that deprecated compatibility path should be considered removed because `msg` is no longer part of the supported API.
